newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: U.S. physician sentenced to prison in Caymans.
newsitem.headline: U.S. physician sentenced to prison in Caymans.

text.p: A U.S. physician was sentenced to 18 months in prison for bringing crack cocaine into this British territory for his own use.

Dr. Richard Milton Steiner, 44, of the Bronx, New York, was sentenced on Wednesday after prosecutors appealed an earlier suspended sentence on the grounds that it would send the wrong message to tourists.

Steiner, 44, had initially pleaded guilty to importing crack cocaine and two pipes when he entered the Cayman Islands on a vacation. He said the drug was for himself and his girlfriend, who was to join him later.

He was fined $1,625, given a 12-month suspended sentence and ordered deported. But prosectors appealed the decision, saying that it would send the wrong message to tourists who violate Cayman drug importation laws.
Grand Court Judge David Murphy ordered Steiner to serve 18 months in the territorial prison, despite Steiner's pleas that a prison sentence would ruin his medical career in the United States.
Cayman authorities said they would notify New York medical authorities about Steiner's conviction.
Local law enforcement officials said tourists smuggling illegal drugs into Caribbean countries for personal use is a major problem.

"Many tourists just don't think drugs are illegal in the Caribbean or at worst it's just a slap on the wrist if you're caught," one law enforcement officer said. "In fact, drug importation laws in many Caribbean countries are tougher than what they are in North America."
